sections.h2: What kind of place is Palatine for a home seller?
sections.html:
Palatine is a mostly residential village in the northwest Chicago suburbs. It sits mainly in Cook County, and a portion reaches into Lake County. The village covers about 14 square miles, and 67,908 people were counted on census day in 2020.

Growth came in waves. The village was founded in 1866 around a station on the Chicago and North Western Railway. After World War II the first suburb-style subdivision, Palanois Park, went up, and the population climbed from 11,504 in 1960 to 26,050 in 1970 and 65,479 by 2000. So much of the village's housing was built in the decades after 1950, and buyers of houses that age tend to ask about roofs, furnaces and basements first.

The Census Bureau estimated 65,842 residents for July 2025, about 3 percent below the 2020 base. The housing figures in the next section show a village where roughly two of every three homes are owner-occupied.

With median rent at $1,549 and about a third of units not owner-occupied, some buyers are investors who lease houses out. An investor can price repairs into an offer, which is why an as-is sale can draw interest here.

sections.h2: Which commute routes and school districts help a Palatine listing?
sections.html:
Commuting is the village's selling point. The Palatine Metra station on the Union Pacific Northwest Line runs southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago and northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses on Routes 604 and 697 connect to the Northwest Transportation Center in Schaumburg. The village has been rebuilding its downtown since December 1999, which added a new passenger station, a parking garage, condominiums and rowhouses near the tracks.

Public schools split by level:

  • Community Consolidated School District 15 for elementary and middle grades, with schools such as Lake Louise, Pleasant Hill, Willow Bend and Walter R. Sundling Middle School.
  • Township High School District 211 for high school, with Palatine High School and William Fremd High School both inside the village.
  • William Rainey Harper College, the community college for the area.

Private options include Saint Theresa, Saint Thomas of Villanova and Immanuel Lutheran, all preschool through grade 8. Expect buyers to ask which attendance boundaries a house falls into, so have the address checked with the district before you list.

sections.h2: What does the weather and ground do to a Palatine house?
sections.html:
Palatine has a hot-summer humid continental climate with four distinct seasons. NOAA normals for 1990 to 2020 show about 37.6 inches of precipitation and 38.5 inches of snow in a year, with January afternoons averaging 28.7 degrees and July afternoons 81.3. Spring brings thunderstorms and sometimes tornadoes.

The terrain adds a second factor. The village sits in wooded marshland where several streams begin. Most drain to Salt Creek, which rises at Wilke Marsh on the east side, while the northeast corner drains to Buffalo Creek and a small piece of the southeast to McDonald Creek. Wet basements, sump pumps and grading are therefore routine inspection topics. If your house has had water in the basement, a buyer will want to see repair records and any permit for drainage work.

sections.h2: Which repairs need a Palatine building permit before you sell?
sections.html:
The village issues two kinds of permit: Express for small, listed projects on detached single-family homes, with a stated goal of review within 5 business days, and Standard for larger work, with a goal of 10 to 15 business days. The Building and Inspection Services Division at 200 E. Wood Street answers questions at 847-359-9042.

According to the village, these projects need a permit:

  • Building or replacing a deck, shed, roof or fence.
  • Installing or replacing an air conditioner, furnace or water heater.
  • Finishing or remodeling a basement, kitchen or bathroom.
  • Adding or altering the electrical system, or replacing an electric stove with a gas model.
  • Drainage work, including regrading and connecting a downspout or sump pump to buried pipe.

Painting, installing flooring, replacing a faucet and swapping a window or door of the same size in the same opening usually do not. If a past owner did permit-required work without one, ask the division how to resolve it before a buyer's inspector finds it.

sections.h2: Does Palatine require a rental license when a house is leased?
sections.html:
Yes. Under Chapter 12 of the village code, every residential rental, including single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, must be inspected and carry an annual Rental Dwelling License. The program dates to 1990.

An owner applies through the Citizen Self Service portal, pays the invoice, calls for an inspection, and attends a landlord seminar while adopting a Palatine lease addendum. The license expires one year after the application date and renews automatically unless the owner asks to close it. When tenants live in the house you are selling, tell buyers whether the license is current. If an investor buys it, the new owner starts the licensing steps for that address.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and recording steps apply in Palatine?
sections.html:
The village states that it has no real estate transfer tax. The taxes that remain are the state and county ones, collected at recording.

Cook County Clerk's municipal list shows the state rate as 50 cents per $500 and the county rate as 25 cents per $500. Lake County's own pamphlet prints the same two rates, and notes that the Clerk collects only the state and county portions. A deed for a sale needs the state transfer declaration (PTAX-203), which is filed through the state's MyDec system.

One detail trips people up. The Clerk's list shows Rolling Meadows charging $3.00 per $1,000 and says its entry includes some Palatine mailing addresses. A Palatine address does not guarantee a Palatine location, so have the title company confirm the municipality from the parcel number. If your parcel sits in Lake County instead of Cook, the deed goes to the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division.

sections.h2: What are the quickest ways to sell in Palatine?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: hire a listing agent, go for sale by owner, or take an offer from a cash buyer. Listing gives the widest exposure but means showings, buyer financing and repair requests after inspection. A cash buyer takes the house as is and can close on a date you choose, which suits a house with deferred maintenance, tenants in place, or a probate timeline.

  • Gather the deed, the last tax bill, any permit records and the rental license if the house was leased.
  • Ask the title company which county and municipality your parcel belongs to.
  • Compare any offer to what a listed sale would net after repairs, carrying costs and fees.

faqs.q: Does Palatine charge a real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The village's own FAQ says there is no real estate transfer tax in Palatine. Illinois and the county still collect their own transfer taxes at recording, and the Cook County list shows 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county.

faqs.q: Which county records a Palatine deed?
faqs.a: Most of the village is in Cook County, so the Cook County Clerk's recording office handles those parcels. A portion lies in Lake County, and those parcels are recorded by the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division. Your title company can confirm which one applies from the parcel number.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof or water heater in Palatine?
faqs.a: Yes. The village lists building or replacing a roof, and installing or replacing a water heater, furnace or air conditioner, among projects that need a permit. Express review is aimed at 5 business days. Call 847-359-9042 if you are unsure about a specific job.

faqs.q: Do I have to license a Palatine house I rent out before selling?
faqs.a: If it is rented, it needs an annual Rental Dwelling License under the village's Chapter 12 program. The license lasts one year from the application date and renews automatically unless you ask to close it. Ask the village how to close it once the sale is done.

faqs.q: Will anyone buy a Palatine house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers, especially investors, purchase older Palatine houses as they are. Expect a buyer to price in roof, furnace, drainage and permit issues, so gather your permit records and any repair invoices before you ask for offers.
